questions.q: In Excel, the dollar sign ($) in a cell reference locks:
choices: The entire reference regardless of position
Nothing, $ is for currency formatting only
questions.explanation: The $ locks whatever comes right AFTER it. $A1 locks the column A. A$1 locks the row 1.

questions.q: $A1 is what type of reference?
questions.explanation: $ before A locks the column. Row number has no $, so row moves when dragged down.

questions.q: A$1 is what type of reference?
questions.explanation: $ before 1 locks the row. Column letter has no $, so column moves when dragged across.

questions.q: $A$1 is what type of reference?
questions.explanation: Both $ signs = both locked. Reference never changes when copied anywhere.

questions.q: When dragging a formula DOWN a column, to keep a reference cell fixed you should lock:
choices: Both row and column ($A$1) — or just row (A$1)
questions.explanation: Dragging down changes rows. Lock the row with $ before row number.

questions.q: When dragging a formula ACROSS a row, to keep a reference cell fixed you should lock:
questions.explanation: Dragging across changes columns. Lock the column with $ before column letter.

questions.q: Cell C2 contains a growth rate. In cell D5 you want 2019 population = 2018 population (C5) × (1 + growth rate). What formula do you enter in D5 so you can drag it down the column?
questions.explanation: C5 must change (each row's population). C2 must stay fixed (the constant growth rate). Lock C2 only.

questions.q: F4 (Windows) or Cmd+T (Mac) does what when editing a formula?
choices: Toggles through reference types: A1 → $A$1 → A$1 → $A1
questions.explanation: F4 / Cmd+T cycles through the four reference types for the reference under the cursor.

questions.q: You entered =A1+B1 in cell C1. You copy to cell C5. What does C5 contain?
questions.explanation: Both references are relative, so both shift down 4 rows when copied to C5.

questions.q: You entered =$A$1+B1 in C1. You copy to D5. What does D5 contain?
questions.explanation: $A$1 stays (absolute). B1 is fully relative, so it shifts one right (→ C) and four down (→ 5) = C5.

questions.q: Which formula is best when computing a % of total, where total is in B100?
questions.explanation: B100 is a constant for every row. Use $B$100 to lock it so dragging down keeps pointing to the total.

questions.q: In a formula that will be dragged both across columns AND down rows, a reference to a single fixed cell should be:
questions.explanation: Moving both directions means both dimensions change. Lock both with $A$1.

questions.q: You want a formula to always reference row 1 but allow the column to shift when copied across. Use:
questions.explanation: A$1: column A stays relative (shifts across), row 1 locked.

questions.q: Two cells in the same column multiply row values by a constant in C$2. The formula in D5 reads =C5*$C$2. Is the $C$2 necessary, or would C$2 work?
choices: C$2 would work since only the row needs locking for vertical drag
questions.explanation: For dragging DOWN only, locking the row ($ before the row number) is sufficient. C$2 would work.

questions.q: What is the result of copying =A$1*$B2 from C1 to D2?
questions.explanation: A$1 → B$1 (column relative shifts A→B, row locked). $B2 → $B3 (column locked, row relative shifts 1→3 wait only 1 row diff so 2→3). Final: B$1 * $B3.

questions.q: Count cells in column B that equal "Metro":
questions.explanation: COUNTIF(range, criteria). Text criteria in quotes.

questions.q: Count cells in column F that are greater than 10000:
questions.explanation: Numeric comparison goes inside quotes too: ">10000".

questions.q: Sum column D values where column B = "Metro":
questions.explanation: SUMIF(criteria_range, criteria, sum_range). Range to check comes FIRST, range to sum comes LAST.

questions.q: Average column F where column B = "Southeast":
questions.explanation: AVERAGEIF(criteria_range, criteria, average_range). Same pattern as SUMIF.

questions.q: In SUMIF(B:B, "Metro", D:D), what does the third argument specify?
choices: The range of values to sum
questions.explanation: Third arg = sum_range, the values that get summed when the criterion matches.

questions.q: What's wrong with =COUNTIF(B:B, "> 100")?
questions.explanation: The space between > and 100 makes Excel look for literal text '> 100'. Use ">100" with no space.

questions.q: To count values ≥ 5% with percent stored as decimal 0.05:
questions.explanation: Excel accepts both percentage syntax "5%" and decimal "0.05" in criteria.

questions.q: COUNTIF wildcard: which counts all cells in A:A starting with "North"?
questions.explanation: * matches any characters. "North*" matches North, North Carolina, Northwest, etc.

questions.q: =TODAY() returns:
questions.explanation: TODAY() returns just the date (no time). Volatile: updates when workbook recalculates.

questions.q: =NOW() returns:
questions.explanation: NOW() returns date + current time.

questions.q: =YEAR(A1) where A1 contains 2024-03-15 returns:
questions.explanation: YEAR extracts the 4-digit year as a number.

questions.q: =MONTH(A1) where A1 is 2024-03-15 returns:
questions.explanation: MONTH returns the month as integer 1-12.

questions.q: Years between today and a date in A1:
questions.explanation: Later year minus earlier year. Use YEAR(TODAY())-YEAR(A1) for years elapsed.

questions.q: Days between a past date in A1 and today:
questions.explanation: Dates are stored as numbers. Subtracting them gives the difference in days.

questions.q: =DAY(A1) where A1 is 2024-03-15 returns:
questions.explanation: DAY returns the day of the month (1-31).

questions.q: In a pivot table, the Rows area contains:
choices: The category being broken down by (e.g. Region)
questions.explanation: Rows = grouping categories. Each unique value gets its own row.

questions.q: In a pivot table, the Values area contains:
questions.explanation: Values = the numeric output. Sum, Count, Average, Min, Max, etc.

questions.q: A pivot shows regions in Rows and Sum of Population in Values. To find which region has the largest total population:
choices: Pick the row with the largest value in the Sum of Population column
questions.explanation: Scan the Sum column for the biggest number, read the region on that row.

questions.q: "How many counties are in South Puget Sound?" The pivot shows Region in Rows and Count of County in Values. You should:
choices: Look for South Puget Sound row and read the Count
questions.explanation: Pivot tables display answers directly. Find the row, read the column.

questions.q: Changing a pivot value field from Sum to Average is done by:
choices: Right-click the value field → Summarize Values By → Average
questions.explanation: Right-click a cell in the Values area → Summarize Values By → select aggregation.

questions.q: After the source data changes, the pivot table:
choices: Needs Refresh (right-click → Refresh) to show new data
questions.explanation: Pivot tables are cached. Right-click → Refresh (or PivotTable Analyze → Refresh).

questions.q: The keyboard shortcut to convert a data range to a Table is:
questions.explanation: Both Ctrl+T and Ctrl+L work on Windows. Cmd+T on Mac. Either is correct.

questions.q: When you create an Excel Table from a range with headers, you should:
choices: Uncheck the 'My table has headers' box
Check 'My table has headers' so Excel keeps them as column labels
questions.explanation: Check the box so Excel treats row 1 as field names, not data.

questions.q: In a Table named 'Counties', the structured reference [@Population] means:
choices: The Population value in the current (this) row
questions.explanation: @ means 'this row'. [@Population] = this row's Population value. Great for calculated columns.

questions.q: To auto-fill a calculated column in a Table, you:
choices: Drag the fill handle manually for every row
Type the formula in one cell of the column — Excel fills the rest automatically
questions.explanation: Tables auto-fill calculated columns. Type in one cell, Excel extends to all rows.

questions.q: To add a Totals row to a Table:
choices: Type numbers at the bottom manually
questions.explanation: Table Design (ribbon appears when table is selected) → Total Row checkbox.

questions.q: When you check 'Total Row', each column's total cell has a dropdown letting you pick:
choices: Sum, Average, Count, Min, Max, etc.
questions.explanation: Dropdown offers Sum, Average, Count, Max, Min, StDev, Var, and more.

questions.q: In a Table, to sort by column Population descending:
choices: Right-click header → Sort Largest to Smallest
questions.explanation: Header dropdown arrows → Sort Largest to Smallest (or Smallest to Largest).

questions.q: The small square at the bottom-right corner of a selected cell is called:
questions.explanation: Fill handle. Drag it to extend a series or double-click to fill down.

questions.q: Double-clicking the fill handle does what?
choices: Auto-fills down to the bottom of the adjacent column's data
questions.explanation: Double-click = auto-fill down to match the adjacent data's last row. Major time saver.

questions.q: To create a series 1, 2, 3, 4, 5... you:
choices: Type 1 in A1, 2 in A2, select both, drag handle
questions.explanation: Excel needs at least two values to detect the pattern. Select both, drag.

questions.q: To generate County IDs 1001, 1002, 1003... down a column for 500 rows:
choices: Type 1001 in first cell, 1002 in second, select both, double-click fill handle
questions.explanation: Two cells establish the +1 pattern. Double-click fills to end of adjacent data.

questions.q: Flash Fill (Ctrl+E / Cmd+E) does what?
choices: Detects a pattern from your example and fills the column based on adjacent data
questions.explanation: Flash Fill = pattern recognition. Type 1-2 examples, press Ctrl+E, Excel completes based on the pattern.

questions.q: The keyboard shortcut to fill down (copy the cell above into selected cells):
questions.explanation: Ctrl+D = fill Down. Ctrl+R = fill Right.

questions.q: Filter applied via Data → Filter does what to hidden data?
choices: Hides it — data is preserved, just not visible
questions.explanation: Filtering hides rows. Data is intact; remove the filter and everything returns.

questions.q: To multi-level sort (by Region, then by Population within each Region):
choices: Sort by one at a time, manually
Data → Sort → Add Level; pick Region first, then Population
questions.explanation: Data → Sort → Add Level. Sort keys apply in order (first key is primary).

questions.q: Dropdown arrows on header cells appear when:
choices: Filter is applied (Data → Filter) or data is in a Table
questions.explanation: Filter and Tables both add dropdown arrows for sort/filter.

questions.q: To sort a column of dates from oldest to newest:
choices: Sort Smallest to Largest — OR Oldest to Newest (same thing)
questions.explanation: Dates are numbers under the hood. Smallest = oldest, Largest = newest. Excel labels them Oldest/Newest for dates.

questions.q: When you filter a column by a specific value, rows where that column equals the value:
questions.explanation: Checking a value = show it. Unchecking = hide it. You keep what's checked.

questions.q: Every Excel formula must start with:
questions.explanation: Formulas start with =. Alternatives + and - also work in some versions but = is standard.

questions.q: =SUM(A1:A10) calculates:
choices: Sum of values in A1 through A10
questions.explanation: SUM totals all numbers in the range.

questions.q: =AVERAGE(B2:B100) returns:
choices: Arithmetic mean (sum / count of numeric cells)
questions.explanation: AVERAGE = sum of values ÷ count of numeric values. Blanks and text are excluded.

questions.q: =MAX(A:A) and =MIN(A:A) return:
choices: Largest and smallest numbers in column A
questions.explanation: MAX = largest, MIN = smallest. Ignore text cells.

questions.q: =COUNT(A1:A20) counts:
questions.explanation: COUNT = numeric cells only. Use COUNTA for all non-empty cells (text included).

questions.q: =COUNTA(A1:A20) counts:
choices: All non-empty cells (numbers, text, dates, etc.)
questions.explanation: COUNTA = count All non-empty. Use when column has text/mixed content.

questions.q: =IF(A1>100, "High", "Low") returns:
questions.explanation: IF(condition, value_if_true, value_if_false).

questions.q: =ROUND(3.14159, 2) returns:
questions.explanation: ROUND(number, digits). 2 digits after decimal → 3.14.

questions.q: =CONCATENATE(A1, " ", B1) or =A1 & " " & B1 both:
choices: Join A1, a space, and B1 into one text string
questions.explanation: Concatenation joins text. & and CONCATENATE produce the same result.

questions.q: =VLOOKUP(A2, Sheet2!A:C, 3, FALSE) does:
choices: Looks up A2 in column A of Sheet2, returns the value from column C (3rd col), exact match
questions.explanation: VLOOKUP(lookup_value, table_array, column_index, [exact_match]). FALSE = exact match.

questions.q: Keyboard shortcut for italic text:
questions.explanation: Cmd+I (Mac) / Ctrl+I (Windows) = italic.

questions.q: Keyboard shortcut for bold:
questions.explanation: Cmd+B / Ctrl+B = bold.

questions.q: To center text horizontally in a cell, you can:
choices: Use the center alignment icon in the Home ribbon
Use the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+E (Windows only)
questions.explanation: Both work. Note: Ctrl+E is Flash Fill on newer Excel, so the ribbon icon is safer.

questions.q: To change column width to fit content automatically:
choices: Drag the right border of the column header by hand
Double-click the right border of the column header
Use the Format menu → Column Width dialog
questions.explanation: Drag = manual. Double-click = AutoFit to widest content. Format menu = exact number. All work.

questions.q: To apply a background color (fill) to selected cells:
choices: Use the paint bucket icon in the Home ribbon
questions.explanation: Paint bucket dropdown = quick. Format Cells → Fill = more options (patterns, gradients).

questions.q: To make row 1 a bold header with a colored background:
choices: Select row 1, press Cmd+B, click paint bucket to pick color
questions.explanation: Select the row, Cmd+B for bold, paint bucket for fill. Done.

questions.q: To display a number as currency ($1,234.56):
choices: Type it with a dollar sign
Apply Currency or Accounting format from Home ribbon or Format Cells → Number → Currency
questions.explanation: Format the cell as Currency — keeps the underlying number numeric for calculations. Typing $ makes it text.

questions.q: To format a column as percentages where 0.25 displays as 25%:
choices: Format cells → Number → Percentage (or % button in ribbon)
questions.explanation: The % format multiplies display × 100 and adds %. Underlying value stays 0.25.
